baseline_note: EEVDF is mainline fair-class rollback. BORE is a fair.c latency patch on top. sched_ext BPF schedulers replace the active scheduler at runtime — they are not 'more EEVDF tweaks'.

schedulers.label: EEVDF + BORE (linux-rg kernel patches)
schedulers.use_when: Rollback path, debugging sched_ext, memory-pressure stability
schedulers.hybrid_note: detach_tasks + migration_cost 300us + SMT idle (0012) active in kernel

schedulers.label: Landlock Adaptive Virtual Deadline
schedulers.use_when: Undocked mixed desktop: Sway, browser, terminals
schedulers.hybrid_note: Primary laptop pick for 1365U P/E; try before declaring EEVDF 'enough'

schedulers.label: Flash
schedulers.use_when: Minimum UI latency; travel mode with plugged-in bias
schedulers.hybrid_note: Higher power; pair with powersave platform_profile on battery

schedulers.label: bpfland
schedulers.use_when: Desktop IO latency under NVMe + browser pressure
schedulers.hybrid_note: ASA io-class expert; good docked-office candidate

schedulers.label: rusty
schedulers.hybrid_note: ASA cpu-class expert; build-heavy profile default

schedulers.label: rustland
schedulers.use_when: Alternative throughput scheduler; A/B vs rusty

schedulers.label: cosmos
schedulers.hybrid_note: Community scheduler; bench before daily driver

schedulers.label: flow
schedulers.hybrid_note: Lower priority than lavd/bpfland on ultrabook

schedulers.label: beerland
schedulers.hybrid_note: Not a daily-driver candidate until local A/B wins

schedulers.label: tickless
schedulers.use_when: Idle power experiments with sched_ext loaded
